appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Norpois m'en ôtait même le désir [d'écrire]; ... gardait une immobilité de visage aussi absolue que si vous aviez parlé devant quelque buste antique; ... ce fut sans me dire une parole qu'il me le rendit [le poème].
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois's cold, deflecting reception of the narrator's confided literary passion, and his silent return of the cherished childhood poem without comment, visibly crush the narrator's desire to write.

appraisal_events.evidence: il n'hésita pas à féliciter mon père de la « composition » de son portefeuille « d'un goût très sûr, très délicat, très fin »; ... comme il était lui-même colossalement riche, il trouvait de bon goût d'avoir l'air de juger considérables les revenus moindres d'autrui, avec pourtant un retour joyeux et confortable sur la supériorité des siens.
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois warmly compliments the father's investment taste, but the narrator exposes beneath the generosity a self-satisfied comparison to his own far greater wealth, making the praise flattering for the father while quietly diminishing Norpois's own generosity as performance.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is left crushed and discouraged, his literary passion withheld any real validation by Norpois's impassive, ultimately silent reception.
The father is locally praised for his financial discernment by an eminent, wealthy authority figure.
The narrator's aside reveals Norpois's compliment as tinged with smug self-comparison to his own greater fortune, mildly undercutting the generosity of his praise.

ambiguities: The father's evident satisfaction at Norpois's attentions runs alongside the narrator's private devastation at the same encounter, so the passage holds two opposed emotional readings of the same visit without resolving them.
